extracted.intended_audience: NIH R21 grant reviewers / research-funding reviewers and grant writers
extracted.subtask_description: Prepare and document an NIH R21 Research Strategy describing significance, innovation, specific aims, experimental approach, animal use, timelines, and resource/data-sharing for a mouse thymus/stromal gene-expression project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Model system justification (IL7R-/- thymus)
rubrics_metrics.description: If this model system make it ideal for the purpose of this project. First, the stromal cells themselves are inherently normal in IL7R-/- mice, and only the lymphoid cells are affected by mutation of the IL7R. Second, the IL7R-/- thymus undergoes profound growth in response to the presence of normal stem/progenitor cells (Prockop and Petrie, 2004)...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly state and justify why the chosen model system is appropriate and advantageous (e.g., preserves normal stromal cells, allows induced growth without myeloablation, contains organized cortical/medullary regions). Demonstrate that it avoids confounding factors (e.g., avoids damaging ablative regimens).

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinct, well-defined project scope (post-natal stromal response)
rubrics_metrics.description: Our goal is to characterize how lymphoid cells induce stromal growth, differentiation, and/or survival in the fully formed (but hypocellular) thymus. ... this is distinct from ... embryonic organogenesis of the thymus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly delimit the biological question(s) to avoid conflating related but separate processes (e.g., embryonic organogenesis vs. post-natal induced growth).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of established methods / minimal methodological development
rubrics_metrics.description: The methods have already been established and documented in peer-reviewed publications, and thus, no lengthy methodological development will be necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argue feasibility by citing prior publications and demonstrating that required technologies and protocols are already in place in the laboratory to reduce technical risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Microarray experimental design: replicates and pooling
rubrics_metrics.description: We will perform 3 independent microarrays for each sample type (cortical or medullary, tissue or lymphoid), and each microarray will represent pooled RNA from 3 individual mice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify biological replication and pooling strategy (number of arrays, number of animals pooled per array) to justify statistical power and reproducibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time-point selection and kinetic pre-experiments
rubrics_metrics.description: We will repeat this entire procedure at key points after intravenous injection ... the points will be chosen to represent baseline, growth initiation, steady-state, log phase growth, and termination of growth. Since the precise timing is relatively important, we will first perform preliminary experiments to determine the kinetics of induced growth ... measure at 0,4,8,12,16,20,24,28,32 days (3 mice per time point) and likely a second series including serial 1-day time points around initiation/peak.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Justify time-point selection biologically; perform pilot kinetic analyses to determine optimal sampling schedule; use replicates per time point and plan for follow-up fine-scale sampling near critical transitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal matched comparison to identify stromal signals
rubrics_metrics.description: Data from lymphoid cells will only be used to identify the stromal component of gene expression in tissue at the corresponding time point, i.e., an internally matched comparison. Once stromal signatures have been established at each time point, stromal-to-stromal changes over time will be evaluated. Lymphoid cells will not be compared to each other across different time points.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use internally matched tissue vs. purified cell comparisons at each time point to extract stromal expression and avoid confounding by changing lymphoid composition across time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Present/absent threshold default and flexible stringency
rubrics_metrics.description: Once stromal gene expression levels have been calculated ... we will set arbitrary thresholds to distinguish genes that are expressed from those that are not. The conventional threshold for this purpose is the median signal value (50th percentile) ... we may also apply different thresholds (40th or 60th percentile) to increase or decrease stringency, depending on the outcomes and objectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt a default median-based present/absent threshold but plan sensitivity analyses with more/less stringent percentiles to test robustness, acknowledging distributional limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations of binary present/absent calls for calculated stromal signals
rubrics_metrics.description: Note that present/absent detection calls ... cannot be accurately used for calculated stromal signals, since they cannot distinguish lymphoid from stromal gene expression in microdissected tissue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not rely on chip present/absent flags for deconvoluted stromal signals; instead use those calls only to eliminate genes not expressed at all in the thymus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flagging probesets with insufficient tissue/lymphoid detection
rubrics_metrics.description: Probesets where <2 (out of 3) present detection calls are found in any given tissue will be flagged, since these are unlikely to be present in either lymphoid or stromal cells. Further, genes with ≥2 present calls in tissue AND <2 present calls in lymphoid cells will also be flagged, as these are likely to represent stromal specific genes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply simple present-call based filters to eliminate absent probesets and to identify candidate stromal-specific probesets for follow-up.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collapsing multiple probesets to single gene identifiers
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiple probesets for individual receptors or ligands (where they exist) will be collapsed into a single EntrezGene identifier using the GeneSet Enrichment Analysis tool (www.broadinstitute.org/gsea).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Map probesets to gene-level identifiers to avoid redundancy and enable downstream gene-centric analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of receptor/ligand databases (HPMR) to identify membrane receptors
rubrics_metrics.description: The Human Plasma Membrane Receptome database (HPMR) ... is a comprehensive database of more than 900 receptors and 600 paired ligands ... the HPMR group has provided us with their entire database ... including MOE430_2 (mouse) probeset IDs that will allow us to easily identify receptors expressed in our kinetic database of stromal growth, and likewise for lymphoid data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leverage curated receptor/ligand databases to prioritize candidate receptor-encoding genes from expression data; integrate database IDs to map directly to microarray probesets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Boolean ontology-based receptor/ligand identification and literature co-occurrence
rubrics_metrics.description: The second approach uses Boolean combinations of gene ontology terms ... together with automated searching of literature resources ... to identify co-occurrence of receptor:ligand terms (gene symbols and aliases) in published literature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct inclusive/exclusive gene-ontology boolean queries to generate receptor and ligand lists and then score pairs by literature co-occurrence frequency; expect a noisier but broader candidate list.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclude high-throughput genomic papers from co-occurrence counts
rubrics_metrics.description: Individual publications citing more than 20 total genes (i.e., genomic analyses) will be eliminated, since co-occurrence in such publications is unlikely to be related to functional interaction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filter out generic high-gene-count genomic studies when computing literature co-occurrence to reduce spurious associations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search both human and mouse homologs for increased power
rubrics_metrics.description: To increase statistical power, both human and mouse homologs will be searched.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include homologs across species in literature searches to improve detection of biologically relevant receptor:ligand co-occurrence and to link to available tools/models.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritization by literature co-occurrence frequency
rubrics_metrics.description: This second approach ... has the advantage of an integrated scoring (priority) system, in the form of co-occurrence frequency (i.e., high frequencies of co-occurrence are likely to be more biologically important, and also to have existing genetic tools).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use frequency of co-citation as one quantitative metric for prioritizing receptor:ligand pairs, with higher co-occurrence indicating higher priority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thymus-specific scoring metric
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the most important [scores] is the generation of a thymus-specific score. ... search for co-occurrence of the receptor or ligand in the context of the thymus (i.e., using the search terms “thymus” or “thymic” or “thymocyte”). Receptor:ligand pairs that are frequently co-cited with each other, but infrequently cited in reference to the thymus, will represent very high priority candidates. Further, an overall score can also be developed, as defined by (receptor:ligand score / thymus score).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine general receptor:ligand co-occurrence with tissue-specific (thymus) co-citation to prioritize pairs that are important yet understudied in thymus context (high receptor:ligand / low thymus citation).

rubrics_metrics.name: ANOVA q value on time-course data for prioritization
rubrics_metrics.description: We will also perform ANOVA on the dynamic (time course) data for stromal receptor gene expression; gene signals that change the most (smallest q value, equivalent to p value corrected for multiple testing) can be prioritized, since these are likely to encode receptors that change the most during the kinetic response to lymphoid cells.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use statistical testing of temporal expression (ANOVA with multiple-test correction; q values) to flag genes with significant dynamic changes as higher priority candidates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expression intensity (decile) as a prioritization metric
rubrics_metrics.description: The decile in which a receptor signal occurs (i.e., the relative signal intensity) may also be used for prioritization; this may be especially important for gene signals that are near the median expression value (e.g., 40th to 60th percentile)...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider absolute/relative expression level (signal decile) alongside differential metrics to increase confidence in biologically relevant, sufficiently expressed genes.

rubrics_metrics.name: STRING protein:protein interaction evidence and confidence scoring
rubrics_metrics.description: One particularly powerful approach is represented by the STRING ... database. STRING can generate scores based on multiple types of evidence; most relevant ... is STRING’s own version of a literature co-citation score, as well as the strength of experimental (as opposed to informatic) evidence. Based on these and other scoring criteria, STRING can also generate an overall confidence score ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Integrate STRING-derived interaction evidence and confidence scores as an independent or combined metric for prioritization of receptor:ligand candidates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of genetic and reagent resources for prioritization
rubrics_metrics.description: Automated scripts ... will be used to parse relevant genetic resources (Jax Mouse Genome Informatics, NCRR Mouse Mutant Resource Centers, the Knockout Mouse Repository, etc.), providing a direct link ... to existing genetic models ... The same approach can be used to parse reagent databases (Addgene, GeneCards, Abcam) for other valuable resources, such as antibodies, siRNAs, expression vectors, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize candidates that have existing genetic models or reagents to permit biological testing within the project timeframe.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clustering of dynamic receptor data to identify phase-specific candidates
rubrics_metrics.description: Organize the dynamic stromal receptor data into hierarchical clusters (k means clustering); receptors in clusters that (upon visual examination) appear to be characteristic of specific phases of the growth process will be flagged ... e.g., cluster specifically upregulated at 'initiation of growth' phase.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use unsupervised clustering of temporal expression to identify receptors with phase-specific patterns and flag them for higher priority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manual curation of high-priority candidates
rubrics_metrics.description: Manual evaluation of high-priority candidates in the receptor:ligand list for those with known relevance in processes such as proliferation, differentiation, or survival, especially in cells of epithelial or mesenchymal origin ... will also be performed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After quantitative filtering, apply expert manual review focusing on known biology and relevance to stromal lineages to select candidates for experimental validation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combined multi-metric prioritization schema
rubrics_metrics.description: The combination of all these approaches will be used to advance a few select candidates to Aim 4. ... co-occurrence score and the availability of genetic model systems, together with other parameters, will be used to prioritize the outcomes ... the ANOVA q value can be utilized independently for prioritization, or this attribute can be combined with any (or all) of the other scores to generate an overall score.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aggregate multiple orthogonal quantitative scores (co-occurrence, thymus score, ANOVA q, expression decile, STRING confidence, availability of models) into an overall prioritization metric; use redundant approaches to reduce false positives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for selecting candidates to move to biological validation (Aim 4)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a few select candidates that meet all of the above criteria (stromal receptor, lymphoid ligand, high co-occurrence/thymus/overall scores, low ANOVA q value, known biological relevance, availability of genetic models, etc.), the path to establishing biological relevance is clear.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require that candidates satisfy multiple complementary criteria (presence as stromal receptor, presence of lymphoid ligand, high composite scores, dynamic regulation, and availability of genetic tools) before allocating limited validation resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experimental validation strategies for receptor:ligand function
rubrics_metrics.description: The two most obvious approaches are 1) viable germline mouse mutant alleles (alternatively, conditional mutant alleles) of the lymphoid ligand, and 2) viable germline mouse mutant alleles (or conditional mutant alleles) of the stromal receptor. In the case of conditional alleles, deletion would be mediated by crossing to hCD2[Cre] ... for lymphoid ligands, or Foxn1[Cre] ... for stromal epithelial receptors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan validation using existing mutant alleles (germline or conditional) with tissue-specific Cre drivers (hCD2[Cre] for lymphoid, Foxn1[Cre] for stromal) and functional readouts (rescue/failure of induced growth).

rubrics_metrics.name: Phenotypic expectation for valid candidates
rubrics_metrics.description: Regardless of the tissue target (lymphoid or stromal, conditional or germline), valid candidates would be expected to have a hypocellular thymus. ... transplantation of lineage-negative marrow from mutant mice into IL7R-/- recipients would be expected to exhibit absence of the induced growth response, providing very clearly evidence of the presence of a lymphoid signal for stromal cells.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define clear, testable phenotypic endpoints (e.g., hypocellular thymus, failure to induce growth in transplantation assays) that constitute evidence of functional relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoidance of myeloablative conditioning where possible
rubrics_metrics.description: This response can be induced without the need for myeloablative conditioning of recipient mice ..., and thus, the damaging effects of ablative regimens on thymic stromal cells ... will be avoided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design transplantation and reconstitution experiments to avoid myeloablation if it would damage the tissue/compromise stromal biology being studied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feasibility statement emphasizing expertise and data-sharing commitment
rubrics_metrics.description: We possess documented (published) expertise in all of the relevant methodologies, as well as in interpreting complex outcomes ... Our commitment to providing the unique data resources generated by these high-throughput approaches to the scientific community at large is also documented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate team expertise and commit to disseminating high-throughput data to maximize impact and community use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project timeline allocation
rubrics_metrics.description: Most of the first 6-8 months of the project will be spent determining the kinetics of growth ... The next 6-8 months will consist almost exclusively of data analysis and prioritization ... The remaining time (8-12 months) will be spent refining the outcomes for publication, as well as performing tests of biological relevance ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a realistic month-by-month allocation for pilot experiments, data analysis/prioritization, and initial validation within the project period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Animal numbers justification and sex selection to minimize variation
rubrics_metrics.description: A total of 420 mice are requested ... The main experiment ... will involve 5 time points, each of which will be represented by 3 microarrays ... only males will be used to minimize variation ... number breakdowns provided for recipients, donors, preliminary kinetics, breeding stock, and potential Aim 4 needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide detailed, transparent animal-number calculations tied to experimental design; justify use of single sex where appropriate to reduce variability and state potential strategies to reduce donor numbers (shared donors).

rubrics_metrics.name: Necessity of animal use justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Animals must be used because we are examining the function of the thymus as an organ, and there are no artificial thymic organs, or any way to recapitulate the function of the thymus in vitro.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly state why in vivo experiments are necessary and why alternatives are insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Veterinary care and monitoring standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Veterinary care is provided by Animal Resources Center staff ... Necropsy and histopathology can be performed according to investigator needs ... Clinical pathology procedures may be included ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe institutional veterinary oversight and availability of diagnostic and clinical-pathology services to ensure animal health and appropriate monitoring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anesthesia and monitoring for more-than-momentary distress
rubrics_metrics.description: Animals undergoing more than momentary distress (needle stick, etc.) will be anesthetized using standard protocols (isoflurane, buprenorphine, ketamine/xylazine). Subsequent to any invasive procedure, animals will be monitored until recovery ... and at least daily for the first week thereafter, for adverse symptoms ... Mice will be treated as recommended by the attending veterinarian, or if more appropriate, euthanized to relieve severe discomfort.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commit to established anesthesia regimens for invasive procedures and to post-procedure monitoring with humane endpoints and veterinary-directed interventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Euthanasia method consistent with AVMA recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: Euthanasia will be performed by carbon dioxide asphyxiation followed by thoracotomy. This method is consistent with the recommendations of the Panel on Euthanasia of the American Veterinary Medical Association.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State euthanasia procedures in accordance with recognized professional guidelines (AVMA) and describe confirmatory steps (secondary method).

rubrics_metrics.name: Data/resource sharing plan and institutional IP delay
rubrics_metrics.description: Within the constraints imposed by the Scripps Research Institute (below), all data generated by this project will be shared via peer reviewed publications. ... It is anticipated that final research data shall be made available no later than the acceptance for publication of the main findings ... TSRI reserves the right to delay disclosure of research findings for an additional sixty (60) days in order to allow TSRI to exercise its intellectual property rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commit to sharing data through publication and presentations; disclose institutional policies that may allow a limited short delay (e.g., 60 days) for IP considerations; specify that format will follow scientific standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sharing of unique genetic (mouse) resources per NIH policy
rubrics_metrics.description: If unique genetic (mouse) resources are generated by this project, they will be shared as mandated in NOT-OD-04-042.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledge and commit to NIH requirements for sharing unique genetic resources generated by funded research.
